newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: FORECAST - Good H1 profit seen at Waterford Wedgwood.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Good H1 profit seen at Waterford Wedgwood.

text.p: Waterford Wedgwood is expected to announce a 30 percent rise in pre-tax profits to around 9.5 million Irish pounds when it reports half-year results on Wednesday, analysts said.

Boosted by an improved performance in the UK following the purchase of Stuart & Sons Limited for 4.24 million stg in August 1995, the crystal and china firm is forecast to show earnings per share of between 1.0 and 1.1 Irish pence.
"The acquisition of Stuart has worked out pretty well for the company," said Joe Burnell, analyst at Davy Stockbrokers.
Burnell forcasts a pre-tax profit of 9.5 million Irish pounds and earnings per share (EPS) of 1.0 pence for the six months to June 30.
He said operating profit for the interim period should be 11.5 million Irish pounds with the Wedgwood china division accounting for 6.5 million punts of that sum.
Goodbody's Dick Watson also expects a pre-tax profit of 9.5 million Irish pounds and looks for EPS of 1.1 pence.
Watson forecasts an operating profit of 11.5 million punts for the six months leading to an operating profit of 40 million punts at year-end.
This compares with a pre-tax profit of 7.4 million punts, earnings per share of 0.82 pence and an operating profit of 10.1 million punts in the same period last year.
"The first-half of the year is always seasonally lower than the second-half when cash-flow improves profitability," said Watson.
Analysts forecast that the Waterford crystal division of the business will have performed better than the Wedgwood china division over the first six months of 1996.
"We expect to see Waterford perform that bit better, partly down to the acquisition of Stuart," Burnell said.
"Waterford will also benefit from increased spending on product development, continued cost-cutting and the introduction of a new tank furnace," he added.
Watson said the company had made some progress toward achieving its target of 15 percent margins.
"There is a bit to go but they are getting near it," he said. "They are certainly much nearer achieving their target with Waterford than they are with Wedgwood."
